lines.text: When holding a plan in your head has become unreliable, build for the bad day.
A handoff note, task sizes, and call lines that don't depend on knowing why.

head.text: Put the details outside your head.

body.text: Not a task list, but the things you'd otherwise hold: reference numbers, what you've already tried, who you spoke to and when.
So does one page per matter.

head.text: Write the next physical action, not the goal.

body.text: "Call the number on the letter" is doable on a low day.

head.text: Record where you stopped, every time.

body.text: Rebuilding where you were is the most expensive part of any restart, and the easiest to skip.

head.text: Sort tasks by how much they ask of you, not by importance.

body.text: Institutions will ask the same questions across four different people, so keep your notes where you can read them off.

line.text: Built for the difficulty rather than the diagnosis, and it never asks why holding a plan in your head is unreliable right now.
